title: Washington Artillery on the Mexican border
summary: In 1916 his National Guard battery went to the Mexican border, where five string players kept playing and were popular in the battery.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Uh, when did you then leave New Orleans?

Well, I belonged to a Washington artillery, which was the National Guard out there, and in 1916, the National Guard out there was assembled and sent to the Mexican border. And, uh, in this battery sea, which I belonged to, were five string music players. So, we continued out playing music while we were on the Mexican border.
Yeah. Do you recall who they were?
Well, there was Souchon, and there was Kleppinger, and there was a Sherman Pardue.
Sherman Pardue played the guitar. And, uh, Bill Gibbons and myself, his father.
Uh, now you were playing very much the same kind of repertoire and same performance that you had a little earlier.
That's right. We just kept trying to keep our hand in. That was all.
And, of course, we were the toasts of the battery when we'd get together and play music, and everybody would really crowd around us and give us a hand when we finished, as you know.
